findings.summary: The case was made in the baseline and asserted in the shipped text.

evidence.baseline: The case is made on the grounds that the alternative, the continuation of the coordination crisis without the attempt to develop adequate coordination architecture, has its own catastrophic failure mode, and that failure mode is structural rather than merely possible.

findings.diagnosis: The whole section turns on comparing two failure modes, one risked and one guaranteed, and the comparison is what the epigraph promises. Structural rather than merely possible is also the modal distinction the volume has been drawing since Chapter One, applied here to the alternative rather than to Providence.

findings.summary: The concession that Providence may not be the best response was removed.

evidence.baseline: Providence is not the only possible response to the coordination crisis. ... Other responses are being developed by other people in other traditions, and the intellectual honesty of the series requires acknowledging that some of those responses may prove more effective than Providence. What matters is not whether Providence specifically succeeds, but whether the coordination crisis is addressed.

findings.diagnosis: This is the volume's largest concession and the one that most distinguishes it from a manifesto. The corpus card forbids conscripting agreement, and a book that says its own proposal may be beaten by someone else's is the strongest available form of that refusal. It is also the passage that makes the invitation of the next chapter an offer rather than a recruitment.

reasoning.note: R-PUNCT-STRUCT. Four em dashes. Three were parenthetical appositives and became comma pairs. One introduced a specification of the design's honesty and became a comma pair.
The shipped label The Case for a Bounded Experiment, which holds the route. The label was not touched.
The comparison of risked and guaranteed failure, the Volume I and II grounding, the concession that other responses may prove better, and the closing evaluation frame.

openQuestions: The restored text says the evidence of Volumes I and II establishes that the present trajectory leads to catastrophic outcomes. That is a claim about what the earlier volumes established, and CTD-0078 governs whether this volume may treat prior argument as evidence. Restored and flagged.

The volume-04 voice card was prepared by the same pass that produced the shipped text, and its exemplar anchors and protected lines quote that text rather than the baseline. The card records `Author approved: pending tone, strategy, heading, and overcompression review`. The restoration keeps every line the card protects and otherwise follows the baseline, which means card and source now diverge in wording the card does not name. R-VOICE-BIND requires that the disagreement be raised rather than settled here: the card should be re-derived from whichever text the author approves.

Structural labels were frozen for this pass and none was touched. Every markdown heading, every standalone bold display line, every chapter label, and every all-capital display line is byte identical to its pre-edit state, in the same order, with the same blank-line separators on both sides. A label determines a section id, a section id is a public route, and `publishing/continuity/section-lineage.json` already records this volume's renames and resolves the historical routes. Changing one is a continuity decision and not an editorial one. Only the running prose between labels was restored. Where a baseline label names its section better than the current one, the cost is recorded here and the label is left alone.

substitutionTest.method: Normalize both texts, strip markup, split into sentences of three or more words, count baseline sentences appearing verbatim in the current section.
substitutionTest.note: Well above zero, so the section is a restoration, not a substitution, and the pairing test applies. Verbatim survival understates fidelity here: every R-PUNCT-STRUCT repair and recorded bounding changes the sentence it lands in, so the non-surviving remainder was read against the diff and attributed rather than assumed lost.

audits.conclusion: The restoration holds under the full twenty-rule index. Twenty-two of thirty-three baseline sentences survive verbatim; the remainder are the thirteen em dash glyphs repaired across eight sites, the credited bounding, the self-reference rebuild, the Volumes normalizations, and the display labels, all attributed. No prose change required.
